key_patterns.name: Layered contact heterogeneity
key_patterns.description: Agents have separate degree counts for family, work/school, and community layers with substantial heterogeneity likely across layers and occupations.
key_patterns.relevance: Layer-specific degrees drive contact frequency and influence strength; use to weight exposure and adoption dynamics by context.

key_patterns.name: Occupation-driven mixing
key_patterns.description: Occupation (Student, Blue/White Collar, etc.) is expected to correlate strongly with work/school connections and moderately with community ties.
key_patterns.relevance: Set occupation-specific contact rates and layer weights; improves realism of school/work-driven diffusion.

key_patterns.name: Age structure and social connectivity
key_patterns.description: Age_group is functionally derived from age and will associate with different typical degrees (e.g., youths high work/school, older adults relatively higher community/family).
key_patterns.relevance: Age-conditional adoption propensity and exposure patterns stabilize calibration of thresholds and habit persistence.

key_patterns.name: Risk perception heterogeneity
key_patterns.description: risk_perception is continuous in [0,1]; typically fits a Beta distribution and may correlate with age/occupation.
key_patterns.relevance: Directly parameterizes baseline adoption propensity and sensitivity to social signals and policy cues.

key_patterns.name: Initial clustering of mask-wearing
key_patterns.description: initial_mask_wearing likely clusters within households and workplaces (homophily/peer effects).
key_patterns.relevance: Captures early-stage Rb and seeding patterns; informs initial condition generation and early diffusion speed.

key_patterns.name: Directed adjacency asymmetry
key_patterns.description: social_network.json adjacency lists may be asymmetric (A lists B but not vice versa).
key_patterns.relevance: Requires explicit symmetrization to avoid biased degree estimates and mis-specified influence paths.

key_patterns.name: Behavioral inertia
key_patterns.description: Panel data with wearing_mask over days typically shows high persistence (P(wear_t=1 | wear_{t−1}=1) >> P(wear_t=1 | wear_{t−1}=0)).
key_patterns.relevance: Necessitates modeling habit persistence/relapse, not just instantaneous thresholding.

key_patterns.name: Information-to-adoption lag
key_patterns.description: received_info has a strong positive association with adoption, potentially with a 0–1 day lag.
key_patterns.relevance: Determines whether influence operates same-day (cascade-like) or with delay (planning/availability).

key_distributions.name: Family degree distribution
key_distributions.description: Distribution of family_connections; often right-skewed with mass at small household sizes.
key_distributions.parameters: Candidate families: Poisson(λ_f), Negative Binomial(r_f, p_f) or Lognormal(μ_f, σ_f).

key_distributions.name: Work/School degree distribution
key_distributions.description: Distribution of work_school_connections; varies by occupation (e.g., students higher).
key_distributions.parameters: Fit per-occupation: Poisson/NB/Lognormal with parameters by occupation group.

key_distributions.name: Community degree distribution
key_distributions.parameters: Negative Binomial(r_c, p_c) or Lognormal(μ_c, σ_c).

key_distributions.name: Risk perception
key_distributions.parameters: Beta(α_r, β_r); optionally stratify by age_group or occupation.

key_distributions.name: Initial mask-wearing prevalence
key_distributions.description: Population-level initial adoption at t0 from initial_mask_wearing.
key_distributions.parameters: Bernoulli with p0; stratified p0 by age_group/occupation if heterogeneous.

key_distributions.name: Exposure rate (received_info)
key_distributions.description: Daily probability of receiving pro-mask information.
key_distributions.parameters: Bernoulli with π_info or Poisson with λ_info per day; potentially agent-specific random effects.

key_distributions.name: Mask-wearing spell durations
key_distributions.parameters: Geometric with parameter σ_off (ending wear) and σ_on (ending non-wear) or discrete-time hazard with covariates.

key_relationships.relationship: Higher risk_perception increases adoption probability and reduces relapse.
key_relationships.strength: Typically moderate to strong; quantify via logistic regression coefficient magnitude.

key_relationships.relationship: Adoption hazard increases with masked neighbor fraction; strongest in family, moderate in work/school, weakest in community.
key_relationships.strength: Layer-weighted effects expected; estimate separate betas per layer.
Strong; high R² in ANOVA/GLM of degree ~ occupation.

key_relationships.relationship: Age group associates with relative contact mix (e.g., youths: more work/school; older: more family/community).
key_relationships.strength: Moderate; assess via group-wise means and effect sizes.

key_relationships.relationship: Positive effect of received_info on same-day or next-day wearing.
key_relationships.strength: Quantify via Δ in transition probabilities; choose lag by AIC/BIC.

key_relationships.relationship: Higher total connections correlate with higher info receipt probability.
key_relationships.strength: Moderate; check via correlation or Poisson regression.

use_empirical_network.notes: Empirical adjacency preserves clustering and communities; fallback to configuration model per layer when missing.

symmetrization_method.notes: Remove self-loops and duplicates; validate all equals union of layer lists.

layer_degree_sequences.value: use family_connections, work_school_connections, community_connections per agent
layer_degree_sequences.notes: Validate total_connections equals the sum; impute missing via group medians.

triadic_closure_probability.source: Derived from social_network.json or set via target clustering coefficient

layer_contact_frequency_weights.source: Literature-informed prior; refine via panel adoption timing
layer_contact_frequency_weights.notes: Normalize to 1; allow occupation-specific overrides (students: boost work/school).

assortativity_targets.source: social_network.json (if available) or configuration model with degree-corrected block model
assortativity_targets.notes: Preserve mixing patterns that affect cluster-driven diffusion.

initial_mask_prevalence_p0.notes: Set per subgroup if heterogeneity is strong.

baseline_adoption_intercept_alpha0.value: estimate_via_logit_on_panel (wear_t ~ wear_{t-1} + received_info + controls, intercept term)
baseline_adoption_intercept_alpha0.notes: Represents adoption when no masked neighbors and average risk_perception.

neighbor_influence_betas.source: panel.csv joined with network; fraction masked neighbors by layer
neighbor_influence_betas.notes: Expect β_f > β_w > β_c; estimate via logistic regression or discrete-time hazard.

risk_perception_weight_gamma.source: agents.csv risk_perception interacted in adoption model
risk_perception_weight_gamma.notes: Scale contribution of risk_perception to log-odds of adoption.

habit_persistence_phi.notes: Calibrate separately from adoption to capture inertia.

relapse_rate_sigma_off.value: P(wear_t=0 | wear_{t-1}=1) or geometric spell-end parameter
relapse_rate_sigma_off.notes: Model cessation hazard; include policy and info effects.

adoption_rate_sigma_on.notes: Baseline plus social and risk effects.

effect_lag_L.source: panel.csv (compare models with received_info_t vs received_info_{t-1})
effect_lag_L.notes: If immediate effects dominate, set L=0; else L=1.

temperature_or_noise.source: Modeling choice to match variance in adoption not explained by covariates
temperature_or_noise.notes: Applies to stochastic decision rules (e.g., logistic noise scale).

neighbor_info_rule.notes: Convert exposures to received_info via probability p=1−exp(−κ*exposures_t).

info_conversion_kappa.value: calibrate to match mean(received_info) and elasticity of adoption
info_conversion_kappa.notes: Scales exposures to probability of info receipt.

mandate_activation_days.notes: Use to compute policy sensitivity metric.

mandate_effect_delta.value: shift in adoption intercept or direct state override in covered contexts
mandate_effect_delta.source: Estimate by comparing pre/post periods if available
mandate_effect_delta.notes: Contributes to 政策敏感度 metric.

noncompliance_probability_p_nc.notes: Feeds 政策不合规率 and 处罚次数 metrics.

inspection_rate_and_penalty.notes: Determine enforcement costs and per-capita penalties.

occupation_specific_layer_weights.source: Recommended priors; refine via calibration to panel timing
occupation_specific_layer_weights.notes: Normalize per occupation; adjust to match observed adoption trajectories.

Rb_estimation_window.notes: Compute average secondary adoptions per new adopter in early growth phase.

inequality_groups_for_gini.notes: Compute group-wise adoption rates and Gini over groups or locations if available.

preprocessing_steps.purpose: Ensure types (bools, ints, floats) are correct; check age_group matches age and total_connections equals sum of layer degrees.
Convert keys to ints, remove self-loops/duplicates, enforce undirected edges using OR rule; verify all equals union of layers.
Join panel states to network per day to compute fraction of masked neighbors by layer for each agent.
Create wear_{t-1}, received_info_{t}, received_info_{t-1}; compute spell lengths for wearing and non-wearing.
Estimate Beta for risk_perception; fit degree distributions per layer/occupation to inform network generation if needed.
Impute missing degrees (group medians), cap extreme degrees, and ensure continuous day ranges per agent in panel.

calibration_strategy.calibration_approach: Two-stage with joint refinement: (1) Network stage—use social_network.json when available; else generate per-layer configuration model matching degree sequences, assortativity targets, and clustering via triadic closure. (2) Behavioral stage—estimate discrete-time hazard/logit models for adoption and cessation: logit(P(wear_t=1)) = α0 + φ*wear_{t-1} + γ*risk_perception + β_f*f_masked_family + β_w*f_masked_work + β_c*f_masked_community + ψ*received_info_{t-L} + controls (age_group, occupation). Choose lag L via AIC/BIC. Convert coefficients to simulation probabilities each tick. If panel coverage is partial, augment with Simulated Method of Moments/ABC to match macro targets (overall adoption curve, time to 50%, peak rate). Iterate to jointly tune layer_contact_frequency_weights, neighbor_influence_betas, and info_conversion_kappa to minimize discrepancy.
calibration_strategy.validation_strategy: Hold out a temporal window (e.g., last 20% days) and/or a random subset of agents. Validate: (a) Macro—compare overall adoption time series, time to 50%, peak adoption, policy sensitivity (pre/post differences). (b) Micro—confusion matrix for daily transitions, calibration curves of predicted vs observed adoption probability. (c) Network—spatial clustering of adopters (clustering coefficient among adopters), assortativity by occupation/age. (d) Early growth—estimate behavioral Rb in early window and compare. (e) Inequality—compute Gini of adoption across age_group/occupation. Perform sensitivity analyses on enforcement parameters to assess robustness of 政策不合规率 and 处罚次数/人均处罚.

file_summaries:
- Data structure and type:
  - CSV; one row per agent (flat, tabular). No nested elements or explicit edges. Suitable as the node/agent attribute table for a multi-layer social network.

- Column meanings:
  - agent_id: unique agent identifier (primary key; for joins with edge lists if provided).
  - age: integer age in years.
  - age_group: categorical bucket derived from age (e.g., Youth, Young Adult, Middle Age).
  - occupation: categorical role (e.g., Student, Blue Collar, White Collar); implies presence/strength of work/school layer ties.
  - risk_perception: float in [0,1]; baseline propensity to adopt mask-wearing and to be influenced by risk cues.
  - initial_mask_wearing: boolean; agent’s mask state at t0.
  - family_connections: integer degree (number of ties) in the family/household layer.
  - work_school_connections: integer degree in the work/school layer.
  - community_connections: integer degree in the broader community layer.
  - total_connections: integer; derived = family + work/school + community (use for validation; redundant computationally).

- Relationships or nested elements:
  - No nested structures; relationships are implied via layer-specific degree counts, not explicit adjacency. total_connections should equal the sum of layer degrees.
  - age_group is functionally dependent on age; total_connections is functionally dependent on the three layer degrees.

- How this informs simulation entities/interactions:
  - Agents: instantiate one agent per row with attributes {age, age_group, occupation, risk_perception, mask_state}.
  - Network: generate a multi-layer graph (family, work/school, community) using the provided degree sequence per layer (e.g., configuration model per layer), ensuring undirected/symmetric ties and matching degree totals across agents.
  - Influence dynamics: compute mask-wearing adoption/cessation probabilities as functions of risk_perception and the fraction of masked neighbors per layer, with optional layer weights (e.g., family > work/school > community) and occupation/age modifiers (e.g., Students emphasize work/school contacts).
  - Initialization: set mask state from initial_mask_wearing; validate degree sums; optionally reconcile age_group with age.
  - Metrics: total_connections can guide contact frequency or exposure weighting across layers.

Semantic metadata summary for social_network.json

- Overall structure and type
  - JSON object (dictionary) mapping agent IDs (as strings) to adjacency lists grouped by social context.
  - Each value is a nested object with four keys: family, work_school, community, all. Each key maps to a list of integer IDs representing neighbors.

- Meaning of keys
  - family: Household/kin ties; strongest, frequent, repeated contacts.
  - work_school: Coworkers or classmates; medium-strength, routine contacts.
  - community: Broader social contacts (neighbors, friends, activities); weaker, less frequent.
  - all: Union of all contacts across the three contexts; redundant convenience field.

- Relationships and nesting
  - The lists are adjacency lists forming a multiplex (multi-layer) social network with three layers: family, work_school, community.
  - all is the set union of the three layers for the same agent (no additional types implied).
  - Edges are unweighted in the data; directionality is not guaranteed (lists may not be symmetric), so treat as directed unless you explicitly symmetrize.
  - Node IDs appear as integers in lists; top-level keys are strings that correspond to those integers.

- How this informs simulation entities and interactions
  - Agents: One agent per top-level key (node ID). Store mask-wearing state and other attributes per agent.
  - Network layers: Build three separate graphs or a multiplex structure using family, work_school, and community to drive context-specific interactions.
  - Contact dynamics: Sample interactions per timestep by layer, with layer-specific frequencies and influence strengths (e.g., family > work_school > community).
  - Influence/behavior spread: Apply adoption rules (e.g., threshold or independent cascade) along edges within each layer; weight probabilities by layer and optionally by repeated contacts.
  - Use all only for aggregate metrics or for single-layer projections; prefer layer-specific lists to preserve context effects.
  - Preprocessing checks: Convert keys to ints; remove self-loops/duplicates; decide on directed vs. undirected handling; validate that all neighbors exist as nodes; verify all equals the union of family, work_school, and community if you rely on it.

- Data structure and type:
  - CSV in tidy, event-log/panel format: one row per (day, agent_id) with boolean state fields. No nesting.

- Columns and meanings:
  - day (int): discrete simulation timestep (nonnegative integer; daily granularity).
  - agent_id (int): unique identifier for an agent; repeated across days to form a time series.
  - wearing_mask (bool): agent’s mask-wearing state on that day (point-in-time, not cumulative).
  - received_info (bool): whether the agent received pro-mask information/exposure that day (event flag, not cumulative).

- Relationships:
  - Grouping by agent_id yields a longitudinal sequence of states over days.
  - Temporal dependence is implied: wearing_mask at day t may depend on wearing_mask at t−1 and received_info at t or t−1 (design choice).
  - No explicit social network structure is present; “received_info” likely represents the outcome of information transmission (from neighbors or exogenous sources), but edges/exposures are not included here.

- How this informs simulation entities/interactions:
  - Initialize agents: each agent has state variables wearing_mask (bool) and optionally an info buffer (e.g., received_info_today, exposures_count).
  - Calibrate behavior dynamics from this training data:
    - Estimate transition probabilities P(wearing_t | wearing_t−1, received_info_{t or t−1}) and relapse rates P(unwear_t | wear_{t−1}, no_info).
    - Decide same-day vs lagged effect of received_info based on best empirical fit.
  - Drive interactions: in the simulation, received_info should be generated via the social network (e.g., from masked neighbors, influencers, campaigns); use calibrated transition rules to update wearing_mask.
  - Missing components to source/generate:
    - Network topology (edges, influence weights).
    - Exogenous info processes (broadcasts) if needed to match observed received_info rates.
  - Data handling notes:
    - Ensure booleans are parsed from CSV correctly (often as strings).
    - Check for complete day ranges per agent, duplicates, and monotonic day ordering.
